data.hypothesis: Increasing the shared source tile from 256 to 512 may halve tile-loop and barrier iterations while remaining within the shared-memory limit; the larger shared allocation and longer inner loop may offset that benefit. This is an unmeasured hypothesis, not a claimed speedup.

memory_lessons.applicability: N-body kernels that reuse source particles across output threads may benefit from shared-memory staging; tile size remains a hardware and workload tuning parameter.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 256-source shared-memory tile candidate passed correctness and reported 0.00113314 s mean time, compared with the 0.00185035 s valid baseline. This supports the tiling approach, but does not establish that a larger tile is faster.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 512-source tile variant against the 256-source candidate using the full correctness suite and official geometric-mean timing.

data.notes: This bounded adaptation retains T1's shared-memory staging and ascending source accumulation order, changing only the tile size. With the existing block size of 256, cooperative loads handle two source elements per thread when a tile is full. The four static arrays use 8192 bytes; launch.json remains unchanged at block=256, items_per_block=256, shared_memory_bytes=0. Validate this variant afresh; only the 256-tile parent has measured results.
